tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.edit-flag.Argu.description: A bound control changes the field it shows.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.$scenario.Argu.description: The data the app's shots and demos start from is written.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.new_note.Argum.description:
Starts a note titled `title` and saying `body` (Markdown) when the caller knows them already.
Started from the notebook both are empty: what is typed first names it. It stands under
`parent` (at the top of the tree when none) and — where a caller names the note it belongs
after (`after`) — at that place among the notes there; without one it comes after the notes
already under `parent`, never at the foot of a tree it does not stand in.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.search_noteboo.description:
The window's search narrows the notebook's tree to the notes it finds, and opens the first
of them: the note a person searched for is the one they read.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.move_to.Argume.description: Moves a note to a place in the tree: at the end of `parent`'s own, or where `before` stands.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.move_after.Arg.description:
Moves a note to just after `n` and every note under it: the place a drop after a row asks
for, which names the row it lands after rather than the row after that one.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.duplicate.Argu.description: Copies a note, with every note under it, just after the one it copies.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.sort_children..description: Puts a note's own in the order of their titles, once, for a branch that grew out of order.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.delete.Argumen.description: Deletes a note and every note under it, as one change a person takes back at once.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.append_to_note.description:
Writes `text` (Markdown) at the end of the note titled `title`, the case of its letters aside:
how an agent or a script that knows a note by its name ("add this to Meeting notes") writes
into it without first looking up which note that is.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.file_note.Argu.description:
Files a note titled `title` and tagged `tag` in one step: what another app writes down of
what it did (Today's morning) without waiting on the note it made to name it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.new_tag.Argume.description:
Makes a tag of the notebook named `name`, or gives the one already named that: the name is
what people, agents and scripts know a tag by.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.rename_tag.Arg.description: Names a tag of the notebook: every note that carries the old name carries the new one.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.delete_tag.Arg.description:
Deletes a tag of the notebook: no note carries the name any more, and the notebook stops
listing it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.export_noteboo.description:
The notebook as a zip, one Markdown file for each note: a note's own under the folder of the
note it stands in, and the pictures it shows in its own `images` folder beside it. That is the
shape the import reads, so the notebook comes back as the tree it is, titles, bodies and
pictures alike.

The notebook as one Markdown document, where each note is a heading one level deeper than
the note it stands under (six at the deepest), its body beneath it and the notes under it
after it, read as one text in the order the tree keeps it.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_markdow.description:
Imports a Markdown file as a note, or opens the note that file already made: a note keeps the
address of the file it came from, so importing the same file twice makes one note. The note
stands under the note of the folder its file's path names — `Q3 plan/Ideas.md` under
`Q3 plan.md` — and at the top of the tree when its path names no folder. Its title is the
document's first heading, or the file's name; the heading it says the title with is not said
again in its body.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_page.Ar.description:
Imports a page another service held as a note, keeping whose words it is and where it stood
there: what `tilo migrate` calls for each page it brings over, and what a person's own import
of a file does without a service's words. A page imported by its address there again opens the
note it made, whatever the page says now; the note stands under the note of the folder its
file's path names.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_text.Ar.description:
Imports a note given as words rather than a file: its title, its body as Markdown, the
pictures it shows and the notes its links lead to. A caller holding a page as text — a
script, an agent, a migration — makes the note without writing a file first: `pictures` are
the files the body names as `![alt](name)`, each by the name it came in as, which the note
keeps so an export writes it beside the note again; `links` names, by the path a link leads
to, the note it opens. The note stands at the top of the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_archive.description:
Imports a notebook another tool wrote: a zip of pages, or the JSON a Notion API page listing
answers. A zip comes in under the notebook, a page under the page that held it, in one change:
undo takes the whole import back. That is this app's own notebook written out, a Notion export,
and what `tilo migrate` brings from a wiki: a page per `.md` file, its pictures beside it, and a
database beside it as a `.csv` that becomes a table at its page. Each page's title is its first
heading, or its file's name; the pictures a page shows are the files it stands beside, a
reference read from the page's own folder, and a link to a page of the archive is the reference
to the note that page made. A migration says where each page came from in its own file beside
the pages, and a page that is imported already keeps the note it made. A listing carries no
files, so each of its pages is a note at the top of the tree.

tl.so.tilo.notes.Notebook.import_dropped.description:
Files dropped on the notebook come in one at a time. A Markdown file becomes a note. An
archive or a Notion page listing becomes the pages it holds, whether the notebook's own
written out or another app's export. One action, so undo takes the whole drop back at once.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.learn.Argument.description:
Writes what the vault says of an item (`listed`, one of what it lists) into its record, where
it differs: its name, kind and tags, where it signs in, its fields' labels, whether it keeps a
note, when it changed and what is wrong with it.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.keep.Arguments.description:
Asks the vault to keep `ask` (its add, as JSON) and writes what it answers into `item`.
Answers why it could not, or nothing.

choice_labels.login: A login: a username and a password for a site
choice_labels.note: A note kept as a secret, with no address
choice_labels.secret: Any other secret: a licence code, a recovery key
choice_labels.wifi: The password of a Wi-Fi network

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.rewrite.Argume.description:
Writes the item as it is, with `title`, `kind` and `places` in place of its own and `more`
beside them. Answers why it could not, or nothing.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.set_username.A.description: Writes who the item signs in as.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.change_secret..description:
Changes the item's password, key or secret: the person types it on the system's card, and the
vault keeps it. Nothing of it reaches this app's code, its records or history.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.write_note.Arg.description: Writes the item's note: typed on the system's card, kept in the vault.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.add_field.Argu.description: Adds a field to the item, such as a PIN: its value typed on the system's card.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.remove_field.A.description: Takes a field off the item.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.generate_passw.description:
Draws a strong password for the login where the vault is: 20 characters by default, with a
capital, a small letter, a digit and a symbol. Nobody types or sees it.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.favorite.Argum.description: Puts an item in the person's favorites, or takes it out.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.add_tag.Argume.description: Gives an item a tag, as the words beside its tags are typed.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.remove_tag.Arg.description: Takes a tag off an item.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.add_origin.Arg.description: Gives an item an address it signs in to, checked as a web address, as typed beside them.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.remove_origin..description: Takes an address off an item.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.rename.Argumen.description: Renames an item, in its record and in the vault.

choice_labels.login: A login: a username and a password for a site
choice_labels.note: A note kept as a secret, with no address
choice_labels.secret: Any other secret: a licence code, a recovery key
choice_labels.wifi: The password of a Wi-Fi network

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.set_kind.Argum.description: Changes what kind of secret an item is.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.copy_secret.Ar.description:
Puts the item's secret on the person's clipboard from the vault, which forgets it again after
a while. It never passes through Passwords, and the vault records the copy as a use.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.copy_identity..description:
Puts what identifies the person to the account on their clipboard from the vault: a login's
username, an API key's account.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.copy_part.Argu.description:
Asks the vault to put `part` of the item on the person's clipboard. Answers why it could not,
or nothing.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.copy_origins.A.description: Copies the addresses the item signs in to, one a line.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.shown_part.Arg.description:
Asks the vault to show `part` of the item for a while, where `how` says (`show` for the
window, `hold` for the host): the name it is shown under, or nothing where the item keeps
none. The vault records each showing as a use.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.reveal.Argumen.description:
Shows the item's secret, who it signs in as, its note and its fields in the window, for 30
seconds at most: each part by a name only the window reads it under.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.access.Argumen.description: Reads who used the item, and the leaves its person gave: what the item's access page shows.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Item.take_back.Argu.description: Takes back a leave the item's person gave: the agent or app it names asks again next time.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.add_new.Argum.description:
Adds a new item to the vault from `ask` (its add, as JSON) and lists it: the item, or nothing
where the vault did not keep it, with why in the vault's notice.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.new_item.Argu.description:
Starts a login: an item of the vault named by what is typed first, with a strong password
drawn where the vault is, which nobody types or sees. The person changes it on the item.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.save_login.Ar.description:
Adds a login in one step: what an agent, a script or the VM's own end-to-end check asks of the
vault. The person types its password on the system's card, so whoever asked never holds it,
and the vault keeps it. An address is checked as a web address.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.list_logins.A.description:
The vault's logins, by name and by the item that holds each: what a script, an agent or
another device's window lists. The passwords are never part of it.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.delete.Argume.description: Deletes an item from the vault.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.settle.Argume.description:
Brings the vault and its items together: an item the vault keeps that is not listed (a mail
account's password, a connector's token, one another device added) gets a record, what the
vault says of each listed one reaches its record, one the vault no longer keeps leaves the
list, and what an older Passwords kept in its own records moves into the vault and leaves the
record. Runs while Passwords is open, and changes nothing when all is settled.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.carry.Argumen.description:
Moves what an item's record keeps into the vault, once, and empties the record. A record that
names an item the vault keeps changes that item; one that names none adds one.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.preview_csv.A.description:
Reads the browser's CSV the person chose into the vault's waiting rows, each marked when the
vault already holds that login. The passwords stay in the file.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.add_read.Argu.description:
Adds an item the host read from a file the person chose: `item`, its secrets each named by the
token the host holds it under. Answers whether the vault kept it.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.apply_import..description:
Brings the rows the person agreed to into the vault, skipping the ones the vault holds. The
host reads their passwords from the file and the vault takes them from the host.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.held_items.Ar.description:
Every listed item with its secrets, each named by the token the host holds it under: what the
host writes into a file the person chose. The vault records each part handed over as a use.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.export_csv.Ar.description: The vault as a browser's CSV: the person chooses where it goes.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.export_backup.description:
The vault as an encrypted backup under the password the person types twice on the system's
card: the person chooses where it goes.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.restore_backu.description:
Brings the entries a backup holds into the vault with the password the person types on the
system's card, and answers how many came in. An item the vault already lists under its name
and address is left as it is, so restoring twice adds nothing.

tl.so.tilo.passwords.Vault.absorb_device.description:
Takes into the vault what this device's secret service holds and a workspace may share. The
device's authentication material and its Wi-Fi networks stay where they are, and each entry
leaves the device's service once the vault keeps it.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.lay_out.A.description:
Lays a document out on its own bytes: one page for each page of the file, in their order, at
the size the file draws it, its contents and its form.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.read_outl.description:
Reads the document's contents, so the review panel lists them without asking the engine
each time it is shown.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.read_fiel.description:
Reads the document's form fields, so their widgets are drawn over the pages and filled in
place.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.read_page.description:
Reads the page's words once, so the workspace's search finds the page by them and a person
can select them, and reads the links it carries.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.read_link.description: Reads the links the page carries: each area it covers and where it leads.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.show_page.description:
Draws one page as a picture at `width` pixels, kept so a person looking at it again, or
another member of the workspace, does not wait for the engine.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.read_next.description: Reads the words of the next page nobody read.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.draw_next.description: Draws the next page nobody drew at the reader's zoom.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.rotate_pa.description: Turns a page a quarter clockwise.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.move_page.description: Puts a page after another one, or first.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.duplicate.description: Copies a page right after itself. The marks stay with the page they were made on.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.delete_pa.description: Takes a page out of the document; a document keeps at least one.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.import_pa.description:
Takes the pages of another PDF or of a picture into the document, after a page (first when
none is named).

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.mark_text.description:
Marks text on a page: a highlight, an underline, a strikethrough or a squiggle over the lines
a selection covers, in the reader's colour.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.mark_sele.description:
Marks exactly the words a selection covers: the runs of `p` from `first` to `last`, both
counted in, as a highlight, an underline, a strikethrough or a squiggle in the colour the
reader holds. This is how a person marks lines of text they selected, the way the words are
read; dragging a box still marks the words the box covers.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.draw_ink..description:
Draws ink on a page: one list of points a stroke, its points as x and y in turn in fractions
of the page's box.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.new_note..description:
Puts a sticky note on a page where the person pressed, with nothing written in it yet: what
it says is written in the conversation it starts.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.add_note..description: Adds a note with these words at the top of a page: for the palette, a script and an agent.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.new_text_.description: Puts a box of words on a page.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.write_mar.description: Changes what a mark says, and its box when one is named.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.move_mark.description: Puts a note where the person moved it.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.delete_ma.description: Takes a mark away, and what was said about it with it.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.comment_o.description: Says something about a page, or about one of its marks.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.resolve_c.description: Marks a conversation as resolved, or opens it again.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.delete_co.description:
Takes a conversation away; a conversation about a sticky note takes the note with it when it
is the last one about it.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.delete_re.description: Deletes one answer of a conversation.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.place_sig.description:
Signs a page where the person pressed: the signature they drew, else their name set in the
signature's box.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.move_sign.description:
Puts a placed signature at another point of its page: its top-leading corner as fractions of
the page's box. It is a change like any other, so everyone looking sees it move and one undo
takes the move back.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.move_plac.description:
Moves the signature `who` names, as the place over its page reports it: its new corner as
whole points of the page.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.sign_with.description:
Signs a page with a typed name, in its lower right corner: for the palette, a script and an
agent.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.delete_si.description: Takes a signature off the page.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.fill_fiel.description: Fills a form field with words.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.choose_fi.description: Chooses an option of a form's choice.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.check_fie.description: Turns a form's box on or off.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.remember_.description: Remembers where the reader left off.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.adopt_mar.description:
Takes over the mark-up the PDF's own bytes carry: its highlights, notes with their answers,
free text and ink become this document's, once per source. The file's own objects are kept,
so a copy saved with them shows each mark once.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.find_in.A.description:
Finds the words `query` in the document's pages: each page that says them, with how often,
as `Page 3: 2`. An agent reads a PDF's answer without the window.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.copy_sele.description: Copies the words a page shows between two runs, as selecting them and pressing Copy does.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.copy_page.description: Copies every word a page shows.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.save_copy.description:
Saves a copy of the PDF with the reader's mark-up in it: its pages in the reader's order, its
marks, what was said about them, the form's values and the file's own mark-up kept where
nobody changed it.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.turn_to.A.description: Remembers that the reader turned to the page at `at`.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.reorder.A.description: Puts the page at `index` where the rail dropped it: after the page at `at`.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.import_af.description: Imports pages after `p`: what the rail's add asks the person for.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.press.Arg.description:
What pressing on a page does, by the tool the window holds: places a note, a text box or a
signature where the person pressed. A marking tool starts a selection instead, which the
window keeps.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.release.A.description:
What letting go does: ink keeps the stroke drawn, and a marking tool marks the words the box
covers, or the box itself where the page's words are not read.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Document.speak.Arg.description: Says something about the page the window shows.

A PDF opens in the reader: Files, the person's own file system and the system's search hand
it over as the file it is, and it opens on the document those bytes already are.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Library.open_sourc.description:
Opens the PDF whose bytes the workspace keeps at `address`: the document those bytes are if
one holds them, else a new one. How an agent, a link or another app opens a PDF.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Library.sign_as.Ar.description: The name typed signatures carry from now on.

tl.so.tilo.pdf-viewer.Library.draw_signa.description:

strokes drawn on the pad, x and y in turn in fractions of the signature's box.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.check_picture.Ar.description:
Looks at where this device stands on a photo's picture: whether it holds the bytes yet, and
whether what it holds is a picture it opens. A record reaches this device from another one
before its picture's bytes do, so a photo says the picture is still arriving instead of
drawing nothing; the window looks again while it waits.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.toggle_favorite..description: Marks a photo as a favorite, or takes that back.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.rotate_right.Arg.description: Turns the photograph a quarter clockwise, as its person sees it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.rotate_left.Argu.description: Turns the photograph a quarter anticlockwise.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.reset_edits.Argu.description: Puts the photograph back as it came, taking every edit off it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.develop.Argument.description:
Records an edit on the photograph and draws it: the device keeps the part the person chose,
then turns it, and keeps the result in the content store. Nothing is written over the
photograph, so every edit can be taken back and the person can see the picture as it came
beside the one they made.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.describe_photo.A.description:
What a picture shows, in a sentence, as the device's image model reads it: the sentence the
library's details show and search finds. The work is the device's own, asked of this session
on the app's behalf, so the app never runs a model itself.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.recognize_text.A.description:
The words in the photograph, read on this device and kept with the photo, so the library
finds it by what it says. Needs no model: a device without one still reads its text.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.copy_photo.Argum.description: Copies the photograph to the person's clipboard as a picture, so it pastes into another app.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.tag_photo.Argume.description:
What the device's image model finds in a picture, added to what the photo already lists: the
objects, and the pets apart from them.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.analyze_photo.Ar.description:
What the photograph shows, as the device's model reads it in one go: the sentence search finds
it by, the words in it, and the objects and pets it holds. It replaces what the photo said
before, so analyzing again after the picture changed says what it shows now.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.crop_photo.Argum.description:
Keeps the part of the photograph its person chose: `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` are
fractions of the picture as the window shows it, so every member and device reads the crop.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.untag.Arguments.description: Takes a tag off a photo.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.share.Arguments.description:
The link that reaches a photo's picture: the address of its bytes, which every device of the
workspace reads from the content store.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.set_place.Argume.description:
Sets the place a photo was taken from where the person points on the map: the picker reports
the point as its latitude then its longitude.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.clear_place.Argu.description: Takes the place off a photo.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Photo.export_photo.Arg.description: The original picture as a file, to save where the person says.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.import_photo.A.description:
Imports a photograph the person picks: the library keeps the address of its bytes, the name it
came in with, what its own container says of it (when and where it was taken) and a small
preview the grid draws. A picture whose bytes the window already holds reads at once.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.absorb_picture.description:
Adds the picture a file holds to the library: the photo the same picture already made, brought
up to what the file says now, or a new one. What the person set on a photo — its place, its
tags — is theirs, so reading the file again never overwrites it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.import_photo_m.description:
Imports a photograph a caller already knows the capture time and place of (the camera's
handoff). It opens no file kind of its own: the `opens` action above is what Files and the
person's own file system hand a picture to.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.import_folder..description:
Imports the pictures a person drops on the window or picks a folder of, as a job on this
device: it reads each picture, when and where it was taken and its preview, saying how far it
has got as it goes, and can be stopped. A file that is no picture is left alone and said so.
Picking the same folder again brings what the files say to the photos already there, rather
than making a second copy of each.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.start_import.A.description:
Starts the device reading the pictures `ask` names, stopping an import still under way first.
When the job ends, `imported` brings what it read into the library, as the one who started it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.imported.Argum.description:
An import's end: each picture it read becomes a photo, or brings what it says to the photo the
same picture already made, and what it could not read is kept to try again. What the person set
on a photo (its time, its place) is theirs, so reading it again never overwrites it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.stop_import.Ar.description:
Stops the import under way: it ends after the picture it is reading, and what it read so far
joins the library.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.retry_import.A.description: Tries again the pictures the last import could not read where trying again could help.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.reindex.Argume.description:
Reads the photos of a folder again, or of the whole library when no folder is named: their
previews, and when and where they were taken where nobody set it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.dismiss_import.description: Takes the last import's report off the window.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.favorite_selec.description: Marks each named photo a favorite.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.remove_selecte.description: Takes each named photo out of the library.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.edit_selected..description:
Changes the details of every named photo as one change: a field left `keep` keeps what each
photo has, `clear` takes it off all of them, `set` gives them all one value, and tags and
people are added or taken off across the selection, so every photo keeps the rest of its own.
The selection is names in a list, so a person's selection, an agent's and a program's are the
same change, undone at once.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.remove.Argumen.description: Takes a photo out of the library. The file it came from is not touched.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.new_album.Argu.description: Starts an album, and puts the photo it is started from in it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.remove_album.A.description: Deletes an album. Its photos stay in the library.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.start_album_dr.description:
Opens an album draft: the album `id` names as it stands now, or an empty one to start. The
person chooses its photos in the library and nothing about the album changes until they save
the draft, so a change another member makes meanwhile is reviewed, not overwritten unseen.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.album_draft_to.description: Chooses a photo for the album draft, or takes it out of the draft when it is already in it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.cancel_album_d.description: Closes the album draft, saving nothing.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.save_album.Arg.description:
Saves the album draft. A photo the draft names that the library no longer holds, or an album
another member deleted while it was open, is a change made first by someone else: the draft
stays as it is and says so, so they review it and save again. What the save does add and take
away merges with a change another member made meanwhile.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.delete_album_d.description: Deletes the album the draft is of. Its photos stay in the library.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.dismiss_notice.description: Takes down what the library last had to say.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.add_person.Arg.description: Names a person on a photo, and puts the photo on that person when the library knows them.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.remove_person..description: Takes a person off a photo, and the photo off that person.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.rename_person..description: Names a person: the photos they are on say the new name too.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.face_scan.Argu.description: This person's face scan, started where they have none.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.set_recognitio.description:
Lets this device look for faces in the photos, or stops it: turning it off ends a scan under
way, and keeps every name already given.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.scan_faces.Arg.description:
Starts scanning the photos on this device for faces, or goes on with a paused scan: the model
reads twelve at a time, and the window takes the next twelve as each batch ends, until every
photo nobody is named on was read. Each face it finds is a suggestion of the scanner's own.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.scan_step.Argu.description: One batch of a running scan: the next twelve photos it has not read.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.read_batch.Arg.description: Reads the next twelve photos `scan` has not read and nobody is named on yet. Answers whether there were any to read.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.pause_scan.Arg.description: Pauses the scan under way: scanning again goes on with the next photos.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.delete_face_da.description:
Deletes the face data this person's scans made on this device: the faces nobody named yet and
what the scan had read. The people already named are kept.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.approve_sugges.description:
Names a face: its photos join the person with that name, and the suggestion is sent, so the
workspace keeps it.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.merge_suggesti.description: Puts a face's photos on a person the library already knows, and sends the suggestion.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.dismiss_sugges.description:
Takes a suggestion away: the face is not offered again, since the photos are not rescanned
into one while they are unnamed only by choice.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.person_named.A.description: The person the library knows by `name`, started where it knows none.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.new_person.Arg.description: Starts a person the library knows, with the photos it already has of them.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.merge_people.A.description:
Merges one person into another: their photos come together under the name kept, and the name
merged away leaves every photo it was on.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.split_photo.Ar.description: Takes one photo off a person, and the person off that photo.

tl.so.tilo.photos.Library.remove_person_.description: Forgets a person: their name leaves every photo they were on.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.play_list.A.description:
Plays the items `items` names, in the order given, from the one at `at`: the queue is what
follows, and the item at `at` plays. The app that calls this fills the title, artist, cover,
source and length it resolves from its own record; the shared actions below move the queue
without reading another app's records.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_current.description:
The session shows `item`: its fields are the item's, so a shared next or previous never
leaves the title, cover or source of the one before it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_playing.description: Plays or pauses what plays, as a player's own control and a media key ask it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_source..description:
Where what plays comes from, as the app that knows it answered again: a video's other
quality, or the address it was asked for once more. The player opens it, and the live card
and another device name the same bytes.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_length..description: What the player reports of its length, once the decoder knows it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.remember_po.description:
Keeps the session's place and the item's as `when` records them. It has no effect of its own,
so an app's action that plays can call it inline: an action that needs a moment is a step of
its own, which a nested call only suggests.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_positio.description:
Where the player stands, as it reports it, so a later opening resumes there: the session's
place and the item's, kept so another device or a later opening continues from it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_share.A.description:
Where the player stands, as the share of its length a player reports (`0..=1`), kept so a
later opening resumes there.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.resume.Argu.description:
Moves what plays to where `ref` was left, so a video or a song continues where the person
stopped instead of beginning again.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.play.Argume.description: Plays what is chosen, or begins again where it stands.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.pause.Argum.description: Pauses what plays and starts it again where it stood ([`toggle`]'s own job).

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.stop.Argume.description: Stops what plays: it plays on no device, and the shell shows it no more.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.next.Argume.description: The item after this one: the queue's next, or the first when repeat is on.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.select.Argu.description: Plays the queued item at `at`, keeping the queue as it stands.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.seek_by.Arg.description: Moves what plays by `seconds`, for the live card's two seek controls.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.seek.Argume.description:
Moves what plays to `place`, a fraction of its length, and keeps the place so a later
opening continues there.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.mute.Argume.description: Silences the session, or brings back the volume it had.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.shuffle_tog.description: Shuffles the queue, or puts its order back. The item that plays stays first.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.cycle_repea.description: Moves repeat on: off, all, one.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.queue_remov.description: Takes the item at `index` out of the queue.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.queue_move..description:
Moves the item called `from` to stand where `to` stands: the queue row a person dragged,
and the ids its reorder reports.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.add_output..description: Puts the sound on one more place: a speaker in a room, or a cast target.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.remove_outp.description: Takes the place at `index` out of the session; this device is never taken out.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.move_to.Arg.description:
Moves the place at `from` to where `to` is: "continue on the speaker" is moving the session
from this device to it.

tl.so.tilo.playback.Playback.set_output_.description: Sets how loud the place at `index` is.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.ask_.description: Asks the engine what the chosen printer reports, so the form offers only what it can do.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.abso.description: Takes the file the person chose as what will be printed.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.prin.description:
Takes a document another app hands over as what this window prints, and shows the print
form so the person chooses the printer and how it prints: the one action an app calls to
print a file it made. The file's bytes are the workspace's content, so the app that hands
it over never needs this window's own files.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.clea.description: Leaves the place another app asked this window to show, so the person's own choice stands.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.send.description: Prints the chosen document on the chosen printer, with the form's settings.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.poll.description: Asks how far the print has got; a finished or failed one says so.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.scan.description: Scans one page with the chosen scanner and the defaults.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.poll.description: Asks how far the scan has got; a page that arrived is added to the document.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.crop.description:
Crops a scanned page to the part the person kept, in fractions of the picture a viewer
shows. The text read off the whole page no longer describes it, so it is cleared.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.new_.description:
Starts a new scanned document: the pages it held go. The change is the person's own and is
taken back from history; it is refused while a page is still being scanned, so a scan in
flight is never thrown away.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.move.description: Moves a scanned page to `order`, and the page that stood there to where it was.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.docu.description: The scanned document as one searchable PDF, to save.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.choo.description: Chooses a printer, and offers what it reports.

tl.so.tilo.print-centre.PrintCentre.set_.description: Prints on both sides of the paper, or one.
One of the printer's own options.
How to scan: in colour, grayscale or line art.
The language text is recognized in.

Reads this computer's publisher key: whether it has one, and its public half. Opening the app
reads it, so the window shows the key's state without anything to press.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.create_ke.description:
Makes this computer's publisher key. It signs the person's apps and their requests to the
registry, and a second one is never made: a publisher key is one per machine.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.copy_proo.description: Copies the proof line: the words to publish where only the person can write.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.copy_secr.description: Copies the key file, for the person's CI: one secret, `TILO_PUBLISHER_KEY`, holding it.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.export_ke.description: The key file, for the person to keep somewhere safe: what they restore the key from.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.apply_for.description: Asks the registry for the namespaces the profile's domain and forge account name.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.check_sta.description: Reads what the registry holds about this computer's key's application.

tl.so.tilo.publisher.Publisher.poll.Argu.description: Asks the registry how the call under way is doing, once a second while one runs.

Takes in a theme saved with Export, from this workspace or another: every role, tuned value
and glass shader, once it is admitted and keeps every contrast floor. Importing names it by
its own name, so what a person exported under a name comes back under one.

tl.so.tilo.settings.move_screen.Argument.description:
Move the screen picked to where the pointer let it go. This device's own screens keep the
arrangement their desktop gives them; another device's screens move together by the person's
shared layout, this device's too when it has only one. A drag too small to mean anything is
not a change.

tl.so.tilo.settings.set_sdr_brightness.A.description: Set how bright ordinary content looks in HDR, from the slider's value in cd/m².

tl.so.tilo.settings.open_pane.Arguments.description: Show the pane a search page names, as the search's own row runs it from outside the window.

tl.so.tilo.settings.show_setting.Argumen.description: Show the pane a setting is on, as search's own row for a setting runs it.

tl.so.tilo.settings.open_manage_page.Arg.description:
Opens the provider's page where a card, a plan and the invoices change, in the app that
opens web addresses: the provider's own page, never a form Tilo draws. The page is the one
the account names, so nothing an app or an agent passes can open another, and an account
that names none opens nothing.

tl.so.tilo.settings.open_invoice.Argumen.description:
Opens one of the account's invoices on the provider's page. The invoice is the account's
own, looked up by its id, so only a page the account names opens and an id it does not
hold opens nothing.

tl.so.tilo.settings.set_processors_room..description: The processors this device keeps free for the people at it: the slider's share, made whole.

tl.so.tilo.settings.set_memory_room.Argu.description: The memory this device keeps free for the people at it.

tl.so.tilo.settings.send_problem_report..description:
Files this computer's record of a problem as a problem report in the workspace's feedback
channel, where the people who make Tilo read what went wrong, with the record's own words.

tl.so.tilo.settings.review_contrast.Argu.description:
Lists every contrast floor the theme would miss with `role` at the control's value, so its
editor shows each pairing under its floor while the theme is tuned. The theme keeps the
roles it admits; a value that would break a floor is refused, and this says which pairs it
would break.

tl.so.tilo.settings.review_contrast_on.A.description: The same after a switch was tried: its on is `1` and its off `0`.

tl.so.tilo.settings.review_contrast_now..description:
Records what the theme misses as it stands, when its editor opens or its polarity changes,
before any control has carried a value.

tl.so.tilo.settings.export_theme.Argumen.description: The theme as a file: what exporting it saves, and importing it on another workspace reads.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.read_cells.Ar.description:
What the cells of `range` of the sheet named `sheet` show, row by row from its first cell to
its last, or their input as typed when `formulas`: what a person reads in the grid, for an
agent that never opened the window.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.new_sheet.Arg.description: Adds a sheet at the end, named `name` or the next free `SheetN`.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.new_sheet_aft.description: Adds a sheet right after `after`, so a new tab stands where the person is.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.set_title.Arg.description: Names the workbook, so it is found and listed by that name.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.rename_sheet..description: Renames a sheet; every formula that reads it follows it to its new name.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.duplicate_she.description: Copies a sheet and everything on it, under a name of its own, right after it.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.delete_sheet..description: Deletes a sheet and what was said about it.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.place_sheet.A.description: Puts a sheet's tab right before another, so the person reorders the tabs.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.move_sheet.Ar.description: Moves a sheet's tab to `at`, the place among the tabs a person sees that a drag reports.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.write_cells.A.description:
Writes the inputs `inputs` into the cells `refs`, by position: an empty input clears its cell.
A typed entry keeps the format it is read in (a date, money, a percent), unless the cell has
one the person set. A `seen` stamp refuses the write when rows, columns or sheets have moved
since it was read.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.set_cells.Arg.description: Sets cells from a start cell, row by row: what a table handed to the workbook writes.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.set_records.A.description:
Writes records into a sheet by column header: each record an object keyed by the sheet's
headers, so a value a record leaves out leaves its cell instead of shifting the row after it.
`row` is the first data row (the row under the headers when left out), `columns` the headers a
sheet that has none starts with, and `key` the header that identifies a record's row rather
than writing a new one.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.upsert_item.A.description:
Writes a record into a sheet by the values that identify its row: `matching` names the headers
and values that find the row, and `value` the cells it takes. A row nothing matches is made
under the headers.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.cut_cells.Arg.description: Cuts the cells a person chose: copies them as `copy_cells` does, then clears them.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.paste_cells.A.description:
Writes the table on the person's clipboard into the cells from `at`: a line per row and a tab
between columns. Nothing on the clipboard writes nothing.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.format_cells..description:
Sets the format of the cells `range` (a code such as `currency:EUR`, `percent` or `date:ISO`),
and their weight when `bold` is given.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.toggle_bold.A.description: Makes the cells `range` bold, or regular when any one of them already is.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.autosum.Argum.description:
Writes the sum of the numbers above `at` into it, the run stopping at a blank, a word or an
existing total: the AutoSum button.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.sum_selection.description: Adds up each column of the selection into the row under it.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.insert_rows.A.description: Inserts `count` rows above the row `at`, counting from 1.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.insert_column.description: Inserts `count` columns left of the column `at`, by its letters.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.delete_column.description: Deletes the columns `columns`, by their letters.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.sort_rows.Arg.description: Sorts the rows of `range` by the values under the column `by`, by its letters.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.fill.Argument.description:
Extends the cells `source` over `target`, as dragging the fill handle does: numbers count on,
dates follow their step and a pattern of words repeats. The pair carries the cells it copies
from and the cells it fills, as the grid reports them.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.fill_down.Arg.description:
Fills the rows under the first row of `range` from it: the first row copied down, counting on
as a dragged fill handle does.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.fill_right.Ar.description:
Fills the columns right of the first column of `range` from it: the first column copied
across, counting on as a dragged fill handle does.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.apply_edit.Ar.description:
Applies one structural change to the workbook and keeps every sheet as the engine leaves it:
its cells, their formats and the cells shown bold, its name when the change renamed it, and
the cells its charts and comments are about.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.comment.Argum.description: Says `text` about the cells `range` of a sheet.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.delete_commen.description: Deletes a comment and its replies. Only its author may.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.set_settings..description:
Sets the workbook's currency, date style and time style: what a cell's bare money, date and
time formats are read in.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.import_table..description: Imports a table, a workbook or a Notion export as new sheets after the ones the workbook holds.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.read_content..description:
The workbook as the engine reads it, as text: its sheets, its cells as typed and the currency
its bare money format shows in. An agent reads a sheet's content without the window.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.export_workbo.description: The workbook as an Excel file.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.export_ods.Ar.description: The workbook as an OpenDocument spreadsheet.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.export_table..description: One sheet as a table file.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.Workbook.edit_cells.Ar.description: Writes the cells a grid edit reports: pairs of reference and input, in order.

tl.so.tilo.sheets.read_file.Arguments.description:

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.asked_on_canvas.A.description:
The person asked on the canvas: the hint the empty canvas says until then has been said
(`Shell.canvas_asked`), and stays away from now on.

choice_labels.gnome: The top bar alone; the overview on demand
choice_labels.macos: A floating, rounded, translucent dock at the bottom that hides while a window covers it, and a top bar with the focused app's menus after the system's
choice_labels.minimal: No chrome at rest; the edges reveal what the person needs
choice_labels.tilo: The dock on the bottom with the bar on the top: Tilo's own
choice_labels.windows: A full-width taskbar at the bottom, always shown
choice_labels.windows_desktop: The traditional desktop: frames floating over the shell, the focused window's own commands in the top bar, and a floating dock at the foot, the shape macOS and GNOME people know

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.apply.Arguments.description:
Uses the preset `layout`: every setting it names at once. The result is exactly that preset,
so the picker shows it chosen and "custom" is off.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_app_menus.Ar.description:
Puts the focused app's menus on the bar, after the system's: what the app in front can do
now, on its resource.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.hide_app_menus.Ar.description: Takes the focused app's menus off the bar.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.reset.Arguments.description: Returns the shell to the preset it was based on, dropping the person's tuning.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_bar.Argument.description:
Shows or hides the top bar: the one control that turns it on and off, so a person sees
whether it is on where they press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.dock_on.Arguments.description: Moves the dock to `edge`, keeping how it is built.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.dock_cards.Argume.description: Docks the cards of what is live in the corner `corner` of the display in use.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_dock.Argumen.description:
Shows or hides the dock: the one control that turns it on and off, so a person sees
whether it is on where they press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_running..description: Whether the dock shows the apps running that nobody pinned.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_launcher.description: Whether the dock has a launcher entry.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_dock_zoom.Arg.description: Whether the dock magnifies the item under the pointer.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.move_part.Argumen.description:
Puts a bar part with the one it comes before, wherever the part stands now: the one action
a drag commits, and the same change from the settings, a shortcut or an agent.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.place_part.Argume.description:
Puts a bar part at `position`, counted from the leading edge: what a drag that names a
place gives.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_part.Argumen.description: Shows or hides one part of the bar.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.move_item.Argumen.description: Puts a dock item with the one it comes before: the one action a drag commits.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.place_item.Argume.description:
Puts a dock item at `position`, counted from the leading edge: what a drag that names a
place gives. An item the person's document does not hold yet — an app running on the dock
that they never pinned, which the dock drew from the shell — is pinned where it lands, so
moving an app they already run keeps it on the dock after it closes.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.pin.Arguments.description:
Pins a resource or an app to the dock, before `next` (or at the end when no neighbour is
named): what dragging one onto the dock does, and what the person does from a menu.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.unpin.Arguments.description: Takes an item off the dock.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.open_item.Argumen.description:
What a press on a dock item does, by the app the item stands for: a window of that app on this
screen comes to the front, so the shell says which window the person is in and the top bar's
commands are its own; the window is the one the item was drawn for, so a press never opens a
second copy. An app with no window open is opened (`session.open_app`), and the launcher
shows.

It takes the app's key and not the item: an item the shell's document holds reaches an action as
a document reference, and the press names the one thing it needs, so a run's item reaches it
without a `DockItem` parameter to fit.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.report_problem.Ar.description:
Start a pick: what a report about a problem is about, chosen on the whole screen. The windows
stand as cards; one is picked, and the report's box opens about it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.pick_report_windo.description:
The window `key` is what the report is about: it joins the report, the picker closes, and the
report's box opens about the window, the person free to point at the part of it that is wrong.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.pick_report_regio.description:
The rectangle `area` the person dragged over the picker — its x, y, width and height in canvas
pixels — picks the window it covers first, as a click on that card does. A rectangle over none
of them keeps the picker up, its outline saying what was covered.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.cancel_report.Arg.description: Leave the pick with nothing attached: no window, no report.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.open_style_settin.description:
The style's own settings, and the two ways of changing a style (`docs/designs/app-language/
shell.md` §6): without an agent, in the one place a person's settings live, and with an agent,
by the same actions the person's controls run.

Every setting here is plain tilolang state with a default (`chrome.tl`'s `Shell` document), so
a person who never touches it gets the style as it ships, and the values live in the
layout's own document, synced with the person's devices, with history and undo.

Each setting is one action, so an agent — the canvas conversation or the REPL — changes it
with the same call a press does, attributed and undoable: `shell.set_dock_edge(shell.shell,
edge: shell.Edge.left)`. The style's settings stand over the shell (`style_panel`), opened by
the bar's style menu (`style_menu`, `strips.tl`): a person changes the shell they look at
without leaving it, as `shell.md` §6 asks.

Opens the chosen style's settings over the shell: what the bar's style menu's entry runs, and
what the REPL or the canvas agent calls too.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.show_style_settin.description:
Shows or hides their being open: one control for both, so a person sees the state where they
press it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_strips_tabs.A.description: Whether the strip of several places shows its tab bar: the strips style's own setting.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Shell.set_frames_snap.A.description:
Whether a place let go on the framed canvas lands on the grid: the frames style's own
setting.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_front_workspac.description: Adds the workspace in front, with its row in front, to `a`, and returns the row's key.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_strip.Argument.description: Adds a strip named `name` to `row` at `width`, and returns its key.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_strip_on.Argum.description: Adds a strip named `name` to `row` at `width`, shown on `display`, and returns its key.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_note_place.Arg.description: Adds a place showing the note at `index` of the notebook to `strip`, and returns its key.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_foreign_place..description:
A place of a kind this build has no document for: it stands as it is, which is what a place
another shell made looks like.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.a_query_place.Ar.description:
Adds a place showing a search for `text` to `strip`, with the two matches the notes app
answered, and returns the place's key: the state a place stands in until the person chooses
one of the resources it found (shell.md §8).

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.recents_of_an_af.description: Ada's opens of an afternoon and two of Mia's, newest first, as the session lists them.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.tab_place_here.A.description:
Tab the place whose window's bar was dragged onto the strip `s` into that strip: a person drags
one window's bar onto another's to make its tabs, and the window's menu's "Move into … as a
tab" runs the same arranging action. The place lands after the strip's other tabs and
comes to the front of them, so the window shows what was dropped on it. A place already in
this strip is only brought to the front, so dropping a window on itself raises it rather than
opening a second place. The strip comes forward with it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.reorder_place.Ar.description:
Rank the place `place` at `at` among its strip's tabs: what dragging a pill within the
window's bar does, as the shell's own `move` with the place it goes before. The strip reports
the pill's place among the tabs with the moved pill taken out, so the tab it lands before is
that index of the others; the last place goes last.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Layout.bring_forward.Ar.description:
Brings the window of the strip `s` to the front, the keyboard in it: the session brings its
place in front forward, as it does for a press, a script or an agent alike. A strip with no
place has no window to bring.

tl.so.tilo.shell.Viewing.show_style.Argu.description:
Shows the shell through the style `style`: a package and a view (`so.tilo.shell:strips`).
Switching keeps the layout: the same places stand where they were, drawn another way.

tl.so.tilo.shell.rename_workspace.Argume.description:
Name the workspace `key` what the person typed: the workspace's own published `rename`, so the
name reaches every device and every list of it. A blank name is nothing to do.

tl.so.tilo.shell.rename_strip.Arguments.description:
Name the strip `key` what the person typed: one arranging action of the session's, so a
script and an agent rename as a press does. A blank name is nothing to do.

tl.so.tilo.shell.decline.Arguments.description:
Decline the question at `key`: its asked record's own `resolve`, called by its address as any
caller calls it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.size_place.Arguments.description:
Gives the place `key` the size a drag of its edge or corner left it at, `size` its width and
height in canvas pixels: one arranging step of the person's, its corner where it stood.

tl.so.tilo.shell.drew_place.Arguments.description:
Keeps how tall the hugging place `key` is drawn now, `size` carrying its height in canvas
pixels as the map lays it out: the free area under it on the canvas is what the person sees
there (canvas.md §1, §7), though the place could grow into it. View state the person's own
canvas reports, never a step of arranging: Undo leaves it alone.

tl.so.tilo.shell.place_dropped.Arguments.description:
Puts a resource dropped on the canvas where it was let go. A place that already stands on the
canvas — the place whose handle was dragged — moves to the point it was let go at, through
its own `position` action, so a drag that ends on the canvas moves the place and never stands
a second one. Any other resource — a message's attachment, a search hit, a row of another
view — is placed at that point through the system's own `place`, which is what an agent's
`place_at` runs. Either is one arranging step of the person's, attributed and undoable.

tl.so.tilo.shell.put_history_away.Argume.description:
Puts the surface away once a recent resource is opened again beside the window in front, by
the same `open` an agent and a reference's press run.

tl.so.tilo.shell.step_level.Arguments.description:
Steps the value of the row `step` names (`1` up, `-1` down), as Left and Right do on an
adjustable row: the volume or the brightness in front, by a twentieth.

tl.so.tilo.shell.choose_launcher_row_as..description:
What choosing a row with a modifier held does: a row the search found opens the way `here`
(a tab in front), `beside` (a window beside it) or `more` (the row's own way) names, and
every other row opens as it does plainly.

tl.so.tilo.shell.choose_launcher_row.Arg.description:
What choosing the row the person reached does, read off the row's value: opening an
application or a window here, running a row the search found, or one of the shell's own
surfaces. A row is only ever one of those, so a raw choice — what is typed with no row
under it — opens the first row the text finds, or searches everywhere for it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.open_surface.Arguments.description:
Open the shell's surface `surface` (`overview`, `workspaces`, `centre`), as the bar's own
controls do.

tl.so.tilo.shell.close_launcher.Argument.description: Leave the launcher: the surface stack goes back to the shell at rest.

tl.so.tilo.shell.toggle_vpn.Arguments.description:
Turn the VPN on through its first profile, or off through the one connected: the tile's one
press, whichever way it flips.

tl.so.tilo.shell.a_style_settings.Argume.description:
A shell of one note in the style named, with that place in front, and the style's own settings
open over it: what a person sees who opens them from the bar's style menu.

tl.so.tilo.shell.query_show.Arguments.description:
Show `found` in the place `place` while it shows a query: the same place, now the found
resource (shell.md §8).

tl.so.tilo.shell.query_retry.Arguments.description: Look for what the place `place`'s search names again.

tl.so.tilo.shell.detach_place.Arguments.description:
Give the place `place` a window of its own: what dragging a tab out of its window's bar does,
as the shell's own `split-right` for the window in front. The place stands in front of its new
window, and that window comes to the front of the shell.

tl.so.tilo.shell.show_place.Arguments.description:
Shows the place `place` and brings its window forward with it, the keyboard in it: what
choosing a tab does, and the same arranging action a script or an agent runs.

tl.so.tilo.shell.move_before.Arguments.description: Move the window `w` before the window `before` of its strip: one place along it.

tl.so.tilo.shell.move_right.Arguments.description:
Move the window `w` one place to the trailing side: before the window after the next, or
last in its strip while none stands there.

tl.so.tilo.shell.equal_widths.Arguments.description:
Give every window of the row the same share of it: what "every window the same" does where a
person sees their windows side by side in a band.

tl.so.tilo.shell.place_widget.Arguments.description:
Puts the widget `kind` where a drag let go, at `at` on this display: the place the person
left it at, as fractions of the room it can move in there.

its own way records, so "Most used" is the same number however the snippet was used.

tl.so.tilo.snippets.Library.remove_tag.A.description: Takes a tag off every snippet that carries it.

tl.so.tilo.snippets.Library.begin_fill.A.description: Starts filling in a snippet's variables: one field for each variable its body holds, emptied.

tl.so.tilo.snippets.Library.copy_filled..description: Copies the filled body, counts the use, and puts the filling away.

tl.so.tilo.snippets.copy_text.Arguments.description:
Puts `text` on the clipboard: as a secret, which histories do not keep and which leaves the
clipboard after a while, when it looks like it carries a credential, so an API key does not
stay there for whatever is pasted next. False when the device refused the copy.

tl.so.tilo.speed-test.SpeedTest.start.Ar.description:
Starts a run: the window measures latency against the nearest Cloudflare test server, then
the download and the upload on the seconds after, and shows the dial moving as it goes.

tl.so.tilo.speed-test.SpeedTest.stop.Arg.description:
Stops the run in flight: the measurement stops and the dial goes back to ready. Nothing of a
stopped run is kept.

tl.so.tilo.speed-test.SpeedTest.poll.Arg.description:
Measures the next stage of the run on the page: the download, then the upload, which records
what the run measured. A stage that fails ends the run with its words.

tl.so.tilo.speed-test.SpeedTest.upload_s.description: Uploads a run's bytes and records what the whole run measured. A refusal fails the stage.

tl.so.tilo.speed-test.SpeedTest.record.A.description:
Records a finished measurement, newest first, and lets the oldest go beyond what the
workspace keeps: an agent or a script may record one too.

Downloads a run's bytes in chunks of a reply the language holds whole, timing them together,
and keeps the rate they came at.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.refresh.Arguments.description:
Reads the workspace's sources again: the registries, Flathub and this computer's Flatpak
repositories, and what the workspace runs.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.poll.Arguments.description:
Asks how far the read or the change running has got, and puts what it found into the
workspace. Runs while the window is open.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.follow.Arguments.description:
The job an app's change is, as far as the engine has got: its row says where it stands, and
what it made is read once it ends.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.begin_reading.Arg.description:
A job that changes the catalogue itself rather than one app, followed as the read is: its end
reads the sources again, so a new repository or an update of everything lands.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.begin.Arguments.description: A job the engine started for `a`, or why it did not start.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.read_app.Argument.description:
Reads one app as it stands now: what the workspace runs, what the computer fetched, and the
newest offer its source makes.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.show_details.Argu.description: Reads one app's page: what its source says about it.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.take_catalogue.Ar.description:
The catalogue one read found, put into the workspace: apps in the order the sources gave
them, each replaced where it stands, and the ones its sources stopped listing taken out.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.read_flathub.Argu.description:
Reads Flathub's catalogue over its own search API, a page at a time, and keeps every app
beside the registry's. A person's language names the rows, as every other source's does.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.read_flathub_deta.description: What one Flathub app's page reads: its own AppStream document and what its build asks for.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.absorb_text.Argum.description:
One app as a source wrote it, read and kept where it stands: an app this workspace already
knew keeps what the person looked at of it.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.absorb_remote_tex.description: One repository as a source wrote it, kept where it stands.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.refresh_remotes.A.description: Reads this computer's Flatpak repositories again.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.add_remote.Argume.description: Adds a Flatpak repository to this workspace.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.enable_remote.Arg.description: Enables one of this workspace's repositories.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.disable_remote.Ar.description: Disables one of this workspace's repositories.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.remove_remote.Arg.description: Removes one of this workspace's repositories, and its apps from the catalogue.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.browse.Arguments.description: Browses one repository's apps, through the system Flatpak metadata on this computer.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.update_all.Argume.description: Updates every app the workspace runs and its sources offer a newer version of.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.add_bot.Arguments.description:
Adds a directory bot to this workspace as the person's own shortcut: its program is verified
against the signed listing and saved as the shortcut the workspace's host runs for them, under
the triggers the program declares.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.block_app.Argumen.description:
Blocks an app: it then appears nowhere in the Store or in search, and cannot be opened or
installed from them. Only the person who blocked it can unblock it.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.unblock_app.Argum.description: Unblocks an app this person blocked. A device's or a workspace's block stays.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.import_package.Ar.description:
Reviews a package file someone hands the Store. Opening one never installs it: its identity
must match a verified offer, or an attestor this computer trusts.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.install_reviewed..description: Installs the package someone just reviewed, after the person read its details.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.open_reference.Ar.description:
Opens a `.flatpakref`: it joins the catalogue as a card, and installing it stays a separate
step the person takes.
Opens a `.flatpakref`: a repository's app, which the source installs itself. The package
review reaches it through `import_package`, which opens both kinds of file.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.open_link.Argumen.description:
Opens a `tilo-store:` link: the app (`tilo-store:app/<identity>`), or runtime
(`tilo-store:runtime/<identity>`) it names, or the catalogue. A shell hands a link here
whether or not a window of the Store is open, and what this returns opens in the window; a
link this catalogue holds nothing for shows the catalogue with why.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.review_runtime.Ar.description: Reads a runtime's exact signed offer, so its page says what installing it would run.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.record_moderation.description: Records the registry's case for an app, as a refresh read it.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.prepare_report.Ar.description: Prepares the exact signed operation a report or an appeal sends, without sending it.

tl.so.tilo.store.Store.refresh_status.Ar.description:
Reads the registry's verified status for the report's case again. A draft stays a draft
until the registry answers.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.retitle.Arguments.description: Sets what a task is called.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.move_to.Arguments.description:
Moves a task to a place in the outline: at the end of `parent`'s subtasks (the top level for
none), or where `before` stands. What is put under a closed task opens it.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.indent.Arguments.description:
Moves a task under the task the view shows just over it in its group, as `Ctrl+]` does; with
none named, under the task above it in the list.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.outdent.Arguments.description: Moves a task out from under its parent, just after it, as `Ctrl+[` does in an outline.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_status.Argumen.description:
Puts a task in a column of the board, at the place `at` among the tasks already there: what a
card's drag names. A drop in its own column only moves it among the column's tasks.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.check.Arguments.description: Checks a task off with every task under it, or opens it again with the tasks it is under.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.add_subtask.Argume.description:
Adds a subtask under a task, in its project and column, and opens a closed one: there is work
under it now.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.remove_empty_step..description:
Takes away the subtask the entry left empty: a field that began one and was left blank is no
step of the work, so nothing empty stands under the task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.due_today.Argument.description: Sets the day a task is due by, from the presets or a day the person picks.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.due_next_week.Argu.description: Makes a task due at the start of next week.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.schedule.Arguments.description:
Makes a task due on a day the person picks. Its moment and its reminder move with it, at the
same time of day: a task due Wednesday at six, reminded at six, moved to Friday is due Friday
at six and reminded then.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_time.Arguments.description:
Sets the time of day a task is due at: the day it is on stays, and a task with no day is due
on the day the moment names. A reminder that was set for the old moment moves with it, as a
day moved by `schedule` keeps its time of day.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.due_clear.Argument.description: Clears the day a task is due by: it waits in the inbox, undated.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.remind_at.Argument.description:
Sets the moment whoever is doing a task is reminded of it. A reminder on a day after the task
is due moves the task to that day, its moment with it.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.remind_clear.Argum.description: Clears a task's reminder: it is not told of again.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.remind.Arguments.description:
Tells whoever is doing a task, or the one who made it, what it is and when it is due: once,
and not of a task already closed. Choosing the notice opens the task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_priority_none..description: Sets how much a task matters.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_priority_low.A.description: Marks a task as low priority.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_priority_mediu.description: Marks a task as medium priority.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_priority_high..description: Marks a task as high priority.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.estimate.Arguments.description: Sets the points a task is worth, or none.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.file.Arguments.description: Files a task under a project the person picks.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.unfile.Arguments.description: Takes a task out of its project, back to the inbox.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.assign.Arguments.description:
Gives a task to someone, or to nobody: a member of the workspace by their actor, or someone
the workspace keeps in touch with by their contact. Who gave it to an agent, and when, stay
on the task: the assignment is the change the agent's own turn is triggered by.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.relate.Arguments.description:
Links a task to another, with how they relate: the workspace's own link between two tasks,
which the page of the task it relates to draws too.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.unrelate.Arguments.description: Takes a relation off a task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.unlabel.Arguments.description: Takes a label off a task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.attach.Arguments.description: Attaches a file to a task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.detach.Arguments.description: Takes an attachment off a task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.open_attachment.Ar.description:
Opens the attachment `attachment` in the app that opens its kind: the file a task holds
reaches that app as the same content both read, never as a path neither has.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.write_note.Argumen.description:
Writes a task's note in Notes: a note named like the task, holding what it remembers, made
from the task so it reads under it.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.wait.Arguments.description:
Puts a task on hold until what it waits for comes, or until `until` at the latest: whoever is
doing it goes on with it then, a person or an agent alike. `on` names the automation that ends
the wait early when it runs.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.resume.Arguments.description:
Ends every wait a task is on: what it waited for came, which `cause` says in a few words, and
whoever is doing it goes on with it. It is also how a person starts its work over after its
sessions were lost too often: the losses no longer stand in a row, and a session may begin.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_place.Argument.description:
Sets where a task's working material is: the folder of its work, and the note its sessions
write.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_budget.Argumen.description: Sets what a task's work may spend and how long it may work, and whose budget it charges.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.set_pieces_at_once.description: How many of a task's pieces may be in work at once.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.session_began.Argu.description: Says a session on a task began: counted, and its start kept for how long it works.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.session_ended.Argu.description: Says a session on a task ended: what it spent and how long it worked are added to the task.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.stop.Arguments.description: Says a task's work stopped, and why, in the words its person reads.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.duplicate.Argument.description: Copies a task, with every task under it, just after the one it copies.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.remove.Arguments.description: Deletes a task and its subtasks.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Task.share_with.Argumen.description:
Gives the copy `to` what `from` holds in its set, its list and its collection: what only an
action may change.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Tasks.new_task.Argument.description:
Adds a task to the inbox or to `p` at `status`: the entry at a list's end fills `title` with
the words nothing else there takes, and the day, moment and person they name, so "Call the
landlord fri 10am @Bo" is a task due Friday at ten, for Bo.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Tasks.new_project.Argum.description: Starts a project, with what it is for when the caller says.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Tasks.add_origin.Argume.description:
Starts a task's work on another tracker's issue: its origin, its page there and its number,
and a task of the same origin already here is that task, so importing it again makes none.
Names where a task imported here was first written: one origin per place it came from.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.Tasks.clear_done.Argume.description:
Deletes every finished task and answers how many went: a finished branch goes whole, and a
done task with a step still open under it stays.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.new_tasks.Arguments.description:
Adds every task of `titles` at once, as one change: none of them is made when one cannot be
(a blank title), so a person's batch is whole or nothing.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.set_status_many.Argumen.description: Puts every chosen task in one column (or project) at once, as one change.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.assign_many.Arguments.description: Gives every chosen task to one person (or nobody), as one change.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.label_many.Arguments.description: Puts every chosen task under one label, as one change.

tl.so.tilo.tasks.import_files.Arguments.description:
Imports files as tasks: one task for each file, under the project `p` when one is named, the
file attached to it. A file of the same name already carried by a task is not imported twice.

tl.so.tilo.lang.today.morning_cleanup.Ar.description:
Clears the finished tasks, when there are any, and files a note saying how many were done.
Both changes are the Tasks and Notes apps' own, asked at their action APIs: what they did comes
back as their resources' next readings.
